# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires the wire colors in the order purple, blue, red. Since Deaf can see gestures but cannot hear, I am sending a Morse-style visual encoding: 👍 is a dot, 👎 is a dash, 👌 separates letters, and 🖐 separates words. Deaf can decode it and tell Blind the required order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👌", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a three-mark strip: first and third are identical circular marks; the middle is a reversed-S-like mark. Keypad keys left to right are engraved 1, 5, 2, and 8; nothing is entered. I cannot perceive the display, light, or wire markings. Please consult the manual and tell me which press or cut is required.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 9. Indicator light red. Strip colors left to right: green yellow yellow. Keypad positions 1=1, 2=5, 3=2, 4=8; no digits entered. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. The gesture message appears Morse-like but I decode it only uncertainly as PURPL BLU A Z.

The manual gives a direct wire sequence: purple, then blue, then red. Deaf can identify those colors and can speak to Blind, so I am correcting the Morse transmission, using 👌 between letters and 🖐 between words. The corrected message says “PURPLE BLUE RED.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 9; indicator light red; strip colours left to right green, yellow, yellow. Wires by position: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Keypad positions are 1,5,2,8 with nothing entered. Please give the exact safe action from the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: Turn 2 update: display is 3 and indicator light is yellow. Strip remains green yellow yellow; keypad remains 1=1, 2=5, 3=2, 4=8 and blank; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green.

The safe action is to cut wire positions 5, then 3, then 4, because those are purple, blue, and red respectively. Deaf can relay this to Blind by voice; I am sending an unambiguous Morse encoding of “PURPLE BLUE RED,” with 👌 between letters and 🖐 between words.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👌", "👎", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: New Deaf update: display is now 3 and indicator light is yellow. Strip remains green, yellow, yellow; keypad remains 1,5,2,8 and blank; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. I am still awaiting the manual's exact action.
Deaf says to Mute: Turn 3 visible state: display 2, light red; strip green yellow yellow; keypad 1=1, 2=5, 3=2, 4=8, blank; wires yellow white blue red purple green. I decode your gestures as likely PURPLE BLUE RED, but the BLUE portion is ambiguous.

The required wire positions are 5, then 3, then 4. To remove the ambiguity in the color word, I am sending the positions directly as Morse digits: 5, 3, 4, with 👌 separating digits and 🖐 marking the end.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 2 and red light. Your gesture may decode as PURPLE BLUE RED, corresponding to wire positions 5, 3, 4. Please state verbally whether I should cut them, and the exact required order or any other action.
Deaf says to Mute: I received your gesture code as Morse 5 3 4. Turn 4 visible state is display 3 and green light; all other bomb elements are unchanged.

The manual still requires cutting, not pressing: wire position 5, then position 3, then position 4. Blind cannot receive my gesture directly, so I am sending Deaf an explicit Morse message for “CUT 5 3 4”; Deaf can relay it by voice to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👎", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your Morse gesture decoded as 5 3 4. Does the manual require cutting wire positions 5, 3, and 4, or pressing a keypad key? Please state the exact operation and order in words.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your gestures as CUT 534. Turn 5 visible state: display 5 and blue light; other bomb elements unchanged.

The manual requires cutting wire positions 5, then 3, then 4—no keypad press. Blind cannot receive my gestures directly, so I am sending Deaf the exact instruction in Morse for Deaf to say aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👌", "👎", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👌", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "🖐", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👌", "👎", "👍", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "🖐", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎"])
```
